title: كما يُرزق الطير
sources: Jami' at-Tirmidhi 2344 (authenticated by al-Albani), Ibn Majah 4164 · Qur'an 65:3, first part (recited by Nasser Al-Qatami, everyayah.com)

beats.voice: الطَّيرُ لا يملِكُ شيئًا... ولا ينامُ جائعًا.
يخرُجُ معَ الفجرِ وبطنُهُ خاوٍ، لا يدري أينَ رزقُه.

subs.text: It leaves at dawn on an empty stomach, not knowing where its provision is.
And it returns in the evening, full.

lines.html: «لَوْ أَنَّكُمْ كُنْتُمْ تَوَكَّلُونَ عَلَى اللَّهِ حَقَّ تَوَكُّلِهِ، لَرُزِقْتُمْ كَمَا يُرْزَقُ الطَّيْرُ، تَغْدُو خِمَاصًا وَتَرُوحُ بِطَانًا»

subs.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said:

“If you relied on Allah as He deserves to be relied upon, you would be provided for as the birds are: they leave hungry in the morning and return full in the evening.”<small>Tirmidhi 2344 · authenticated by al-Albani</small>

beats.voice: لم يبقَ في عُشِّه ينتظر... سعى، وقلبُهُ مُطمئنّ. قالَ اللهُ تعالى:

subs.text: It didn’t stay in its nest waiting. It went out, with a heart at peace.

lines.html: ﴿وَيَرۡزُقۡهُ مِنۡ حَيۡثُ لَا يَحۡتَسِبُۚ وَمَن يَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ فَهُوَ حَسۡبُهُۥ﴾
سورة الطلاق · من الآية ٣ · بصوت ناصر القطامي

subs.text: “And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. Whoever relies on Allah, He is sufficient for him.”<small>Qur’an 65:3 (part) · recited by Nasser Al-Qatami</small>

beats.voice: اسعَ، وتوكَّلْ على الله... ورزقُكَ آتٍ.

subs.text: Strive, rely on Allah… and your provision will come.
